﴿By the fig and the olive,﴾ Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, Ibrahim, Ata ibn Abi Rabah, Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it is your fig [this] [[Omitted in manuscript B.]] that you eat, and your olive [this] from which you press oil.

It has been said: He singled out the fig for the oath because it is a fruit that is pure, with no pit (ajam) in it, resembling the fruits of Paradise. He singled out the olive because of the abundance of its benefits, and because it is a blessed tree, as mentioned in the hadith, and it yields fruit and oil that is suitable for seasoning (al-istibagh) and for lamp fuel (al-istibah).

And ʿIkrimah said: they are two mountains. Qatadah said: "the fig" is the mountain on which Damascus stands, and "the olive" is the mountain on which Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) stands, because they grow figs and olives.

Al-Dahhak said: they are two mosques in the Levant. Ibn Zayd said: "the fig" is the Mosque of Damascus, and "the olive" is the Mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: "the fig" is the mosque of the People of the Cave, and "the olive" is the mosque of Iliya.

﴿And Mount Sinai,﴾ meaning the mountain on which Allah spoke to Musa, peace be upon him. We have mentioned its meaning at His words: "a tree that grows out of Mount Sinai" [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/414.]] [al-Mu'minun: 20].

﴿And this secure land,﴾ meaning the safest, namely Mecca, where people are safe in the pre-Islamic period and in Islam. All of these are oaths, and the thing sworn to is His saying:

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 95, verse 4–6:

﴿Indeed, We created man in the best of stature.﴾ That is: in the most balanced of forms and the best of shapes. This is because He created every animal bent over toward its face, except man, whom He created erect of stature, taking his food in his hand, adorned with intellect (ʿaql) and discernment (tamyīz).

﴿Then We returned him to the lowest of the low.﴾ He means: to decrepitude (al-haram) and the most abject age (arhal al-ʿumr), so that his intellect diminishes and his body weakens. The "lowest" (al-sāfilūn) are the weak, the chronically ill, and the children. So the aged old man is lower than all of these. ["Asfala sāfilīn" is indefinite (nakira) and encompasses the whole category, just as you say: "So-and-so is the most generous of standing people (aknaru qāʾimin)." When you make it definite, you say: "the most generous of the standing ones (aknaru al-qāʾimīn)." In the Codex of ʿAbd Allah it reads "asfala al-sāfilīn."]

Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Mujahid said: it means "Then We returned him to the Fire," that is, to the lowest of the low, because Jahannam has some levels lower than others.

Abu al-ʿAliyah said: it means to the Fire, in the worst of forms, in the form of a pig. Then He made an exception, saying: ﴿Except those who believe﴾ [for they are not returned to the Fire. Whoever holds the first view says: We returned him to the lowest of the low, so their intellects depart and their deeds are cut off, and no good deed is recorded for them, except for those who believe].

﴿And do righteous deeds﴾ — for it is recorded for them after decrepitude and senility, like what they used to do in youth and health.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: They are a group who were returned to the most abject age during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so Allah the Exalted revealed their excuse, and informed that they will have the reward of what they did before their intellects departed. [See: al-Tabari: 30/247; al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/557, where it is also attributed to ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim.]

ʿIkrimah said: His old age did not harm this elder, since Allah concluded his life with the best of what he used to do. [Narrated by al-Tabari: 30/244.]

ʿAsim al-Ahwal narrated from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "Except those who believe and do righteous deeds," he said: "Except those who [believed]" [addition from "b"] recited the Qur'an, and he said: Whoever recites the Qur'an is not returned to the most abject age. [Authenticated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 2/528–529, and al-Dhahabi agreed; al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/558 added its attribution to al-Bayhaqi in Shuʿab al-Iman.]

﴿For them is a reward never to be cut off﴾ — not interrupted, because it is recorded for them like the righteous deeds they used to do. Al-Dahhak said: a reward without deeds.

Then he said, as a confirmation of the proof:
